learningObjectives: Define API, Webservice, and XML in your own words.
Name the two main Webservice implementation methods (SOAP and REST) and the HTTP methods they leverage.
Identify the two Systems Under Test (SUTs) used in this course and why two are needed.
Generate and understand the purpose of the Service Access Key used to authenticate against the training coffeeshop.

elements.description: The messenger program used to interact with an application. Unlike a UI, which is designed to be human-readable, an API is machine-readable — it speaks the language of the software directly.

elements.text: A computer mouse is a physical API: clicking left or right is a physical action, but the interaction with the computer happens through an API, and the response appears on screen — even though you never touched the underlying code.

elements.description: A service offered by one electronic device to enable communication with other electronic devices via the World Wide Web. When a social media platform shows a map or an ad without writing that code itself, it has outsourced the job to a Webservice via an API request.

elements.text: APIs are broader than Webservices: a Webservice is specifically the network-dependent subset of APIs (it requires a network to operate), while APIs in general can also be local/native and not require a network at all.

bulletPoints: API = Application Programming Interface — the interface an application exposes for other software, not for humans.
Webservices are the network-dependent category of APIs; this course focuses on Webservices reached over HTTP.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: SOAP vs. REST and HTTP Methods

elements.description: The two main Webservice implementation methods covered in this course. Both use the same underlying protocol, HTTP, but leverage it differently and support different message formats.

rows: Requests data from a specified resource
Submits data to be processed to a specified resource
Same as GET but returns only HTTP headers and no document body
Uploads a representation of the specified URI (updates an existing entry)

elements.text: SOAP (Simple Object Access Protocol) uses only the POST method — every action, whatever it needs to do, must be translated into a POST. REST (Representational State Transfer) can leverage all conventional HTTP methods directly (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, ...).

Message format is another key difference: SOAP uses only XML, while REST can work with a wider array of formats (XML, JSON, plain text). This makes REST more flexible, though SOAP remains extremely widespread in enterprise systems.

bulletPoints: SOAP = POST only, XML only. REST = all HTTP methods, multiple formats (XML/JSON/text).
POST creates a new entry; PUT updates an existing one — this distinction matters when choosing a Method in the API Scan.

elements.description: A markup language, much like HTML, that defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable. XML is self-descriptive and designed to store and transport data, and it simplifies data sharing and platform changes.

bulletPoints: XML underpins SOAP messages and is also used as a standalone data/document format (e.g. an offline address book or product catalog).

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The Systems Under Test (SUTs) for This Course

elements.term: Two SUTs, one per Webservice method
elements.description: This course needs two Systems Under Test — one for each Webservice implementation method being tested.

rows: The same SUT used in Automation Specialist Level 1 & 2.
An in-development app for designing and ordering a custom coffee. Requires a Service Access Key/token to access.

elements.description: A token required to authenticate against the Coffeeshop REST service, generated at http://webservice.toscacloud.com/training. The key creates a temporary (24-hour) profile pre-loaded with basic data that you can freely add to and edit without disrupting other users.

elements.text: The Service Access Key expires after 24 hours. If more than 24 hours pass while working through the REST section, generate a new key — and watch for accidentally copying a stray space along with the key, which causes a 'Key not recognized' error in Swagger, the API Scan, and Tosca Commander alike.

bulletPoints: DemoWebShop = SOAP SUT (same one from AS1/AS2). Coffeeshop = REST SUT (new for this course).
The Coffeeshop's per-user key/token requirement is representative of how most real REST services authenticate.
Save the Service Access Key to a text file in your course folder so it's easy to paste without extra spaces.

examPitfalls.title: Mixing up SOAP and REST's HTTP method support
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates think REST is limited to POST like SOAP, or that SOAP can use GET/PUT/DELETE directly.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: SOAP only leverages POST for every operation. REST can use all conventional HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) directly.

examPitfalls.title: Mixing up SOAP and REST's supported formats
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume both SOAP and REST support the same range of message formats.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: SOAP only uses XML. REST supports a wider range of formats, including XML, JSON, and plain text — making REST more flexible.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming a Webservice and an API are the same thing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates use 'API' and 'Webservice' interchangeably in scenario questions about network dependency.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A Webservice specifically requires a network to operate; it is the network-dependent subset of the broader API category, which also includes non-networked/local interfaces.

examPitfalls.title: Forgetting the Service Access Key expires
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume a Service Access Key generated once will work throughout the entire course.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Service Access Key expires after 24 hours. Any REST work that spans more than a day requires regenerating the key at webservice.toscacloud.com/training.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which HTTP method(s) does SOAP use to perform all of its operations?

options.text: GET only
POST only
GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE
SOAP does not use HTTP

practiceQuiz.hint: Whatever the action, SOAP has to translate it into one specific verb.
practiceQuiz.rationale: SOAP uses only POST as its leverage method on HTTP — every action needed from the implementation is translated into a POST request. REST, by contrast, can use all conventional HTTP methods directly.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which message format(s) can REST work with?

options.text: XML only
JSON only
A wider array of formats, such as XML, JSON, and plain text
REST cannot carry a message body

practiceQuiz.hint: This is one of the reasons REST is considered more flexible than SOAP.
practiceQuiz.rationale: REST supports a wider array of message formats (XML, JSON, text, and more), while SOAP is limited to XML only. This flexibility is a key differentiator between the two implementation methods.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which System Under Test is used for the SOAP lessons in this course?

options.text: The Coffeeshop
The DemoWebShop, the same SUT used in AS1 and AS2
A brand-new banking demo application
No SUT is needed for SOAP lessons

practiceQuiz.hint: You should already recognize it from Automation Specialist Level 1 & 2.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The SOAP lessons reuse the DemoWebShop (demowebshop.tricentis.com), the exact same SUT used throughout AS1 and AS2. The Coffeeshop is used instead for the REST lessons.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is required to access and interact with the Coffeeshop REST service used in this course?

options.text: A username and password only, like the DemoWebShop
A Service Access Key (token), generated at webservice.toscacloud.com/training, valid for 24 hours
No authentication is required
A one-time key that never expires

practiceQuiz.hint: The token creates a temporary, per-user profile — and it doesn't last forever.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Coffeeshop requires a Service Access Key/token, generated at webservice.toscacloud.com/training, which creates a temporary 24-hour profile. The key must be regenerated if more than 24 hours pass.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A learner pastes their Service Access Key into the API Scan and receives an error saying the key is not recognized. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The API Scan does not support authentication keys.
A stray space was copied along with the key, or the 24-hour key has expired.
The key only works in Swagger, never in the API Scan.
Service Access Keys cannot be used with POST requests.

practiceQuiz.hint: Two very mundane causes account for almost every 'key not recognized' error.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The most common causes of a 'Key not recognized' error are an accidentally copied blank/space character alongside the key, or the key's 24-hour validity window having expired. This applies equally in Swagger, the API Scan, and Tosca Commander.

quickRecap.value: Application Programming Interface — machine-readable interface for interacting with an application, not a human-facing UI.
The network-dependent subset of APIs — a service reached over the web (this course: over HTTP).
Only leverages HTTP POST; only supports XML messages.
Leverages GET/POST/PUT/DELETE directly; supports XML, JSON, text, and more.
Human- and machine-readable markup language for storing/transporting data — underlies SOAP and standalone data files alike.
DemoWebShop (SOAP, reused from AS1/AS2) and Coffeeshop (REST, new, token-based auth).
Generated at webservice.toscacloud.com/training; valid 24 hours; save it to a text file to avoid paste errors.
